terms.definition: A keyword you add to a function to say that it can fail and send back an error.

terms.ko: try: 실패할 수 있는 함수를 호출할 때 앞에 붙이는 키워드
terms.definition: A keyword you write before a call to a function that can fail, to show you know it might send back an error.

terms.definition: A statement that runs code that might fail and lets you handle the error if one happens.

landscape.hook: Can you explain throws, try and do-catch in English?

facebook.caption:
Hi everyone! Day 12 of iOS Daily English is about error handling in Swift.

Today's 3 terms:
- throws: a keyword that says a function can fail and send back an error
- try: goes before a call to a function that can fail
- do-catch: runs risky code and lets you handle the error

한국어로 한 줄씩:
- throws: 함수가 에러를 던질 수 있다는 표시
- try: 실패할 수 있는 함수를 호출할 때 앞에 붙이는 키워드
- do-catch: 에러를 잡아서 처리하는 구문

Each example is read twice, so you can say it out loud with me.

Try the quiz and answer 1/2/3 in the comments. I reply to every comment!

dialogue.title: Hotfix call: the app crashes on bad data
dialogue.setting: Hotfix call after a crash alert

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, are you there? The crash alert says the app dies when it cannot read the saved age.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. I see it. We read the age and force it, so the app crashes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Reading can fail, so the function should say that. Mark it as throws.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay. I add throws after the parentheses. So the function can fail and send back an error.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. Now every caller must deal with the error. Swift forces it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Xcode shows an error at the call now. It says the call can throw.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Add try before the call. It shows that you know it might fail.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I added try, but I still get an error.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Because try alone is not enough. Where is the call?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In a button action. It does not throw anything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then wrap it in a do-catch. The code in do runs, and the catch handles the error.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I see. So a do-catch is the place where the error stops.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. In the catch block, show an alert, and log the error.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Should I use try with a question mark instead? It is shorter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That drops the error and gives you nil. Use it only when you do not care why it failed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fair. Here we care, so I keep the do-catch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. Build it, and test with a broken file.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No crash now. A throws function, a try on the call, and a do-catch. Ship it.
